blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — occupational bloodborne-pathogen vaccination
stem: A healthcare employee is newly assigned to duties with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material. Which employer action follows OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard?

options.A: Offer hepatitis B vaccination after required training and within 10 working days of initial assignment, at no cost, unless a stated exception applies.
options.B: Require hepatitis B antibody screening after training, then offer vaccination within 10 working days at no cost when the screening result shows no immunity.
options.C: Wait for a documented blood or body-fluid exposure incident, then offer hepatitis B vaccination at no cost as part of the employee's postexposure follow-up.
options.D: Offer hepatitis B vaccination within 10 working days of assignment but charge the employee when vaccination occurs before any documented exposure incident.

rationale: A is correct. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires employers to make hepatitis B vaccine and the vaccination series available to employees with occupational exposure at no cost. The vaccination must be made available after required training and within 10 working days of initial assignment unless the employee previously completed the series, testing has demonstrated immunity, or vaccination is medically contraindicated. B is incorrect because OSHA prohibits making prescreening a prerequisite for vaccination. C incorrectly delays vaccination until an exposure incident. D conflicts with the requirement that the vaccine and vaccination series be available at no cost.
educational_objective: Recognize OSHA requirements for timely, no-cost hepatitis B vaccination for employees with occupational blood or OPIM exposure, including the prohibition on mandatory prescreening.
source_organization: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: 29 CFR 1910.1030 — Bloodborne Pathogens; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan

option_audit.A: Correct; matches OSHA timing, no-cost requirement, and recognized exceptions.
option_audit.B: Plausible immunity-screening workflow but incorrect because prescreening cannot be required as a prerequisite to vaccination.
option_audit.C: Plausible postexposure framing but incorrect because the vaccination offer is tied to occupational exposure assignment, not a first exposure incident.
option_audit.D: Plausible cost-sharing error but incorrect because the vaccine and vaccination series must be made available at no cost.
